# Compound shard-key prefix targeting

# Compound shard-key prefix targeting — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Compound shard-key prefix targeting. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-30 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] Treat a multi-shard explain plan as evidence of fan-out, not automatic evidence of a missing prefix: targeted operations may legitimately contact several shards. Inspect actual shard participation when checking isolation. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-compound-shard-keys/view

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Design inference: for tenant-scoped reads, putting tenantId first in {tenantId: 1, entityId: 1} makes the tenant predicate available for prefix targeting; adding entityId alone does not supply that leading prefix. Choose field order from common query predicates rather than only from document cardinality. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/choosing-a-good-sharding-key-in-mongodb-and-mysql/, https://github.com/yorkie-team/yorkie/blob/main/docs/design/mongodb-sharding.md
- [statement] Design inference: verify the actual contacted shards for representative prefix queries and deployed data placement instead of assuming an efficient local index or a selective-looking filter proves single-shard routing. Mongos merges results from its targeted shards, so broader fan-out adds distributed work. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/choosing-a-good-sharding-key-in-mongodb-and-mysql/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For shard key {a:1,b:1,c:1}, {a} and {a,b} are leading prefixes that mongos can use to target a shard or set of shards; the full key also supports targeting. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-compound-shard-keys/view, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md
- [statement] A prefix predicate does not guarantee a single-shard read. Depending on data distribution and predicate selectivity, matching ranges may reside on multiple shards, and even a query containing shard-key fields may require a broadcast. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md, https://github.com/yorkie-team/yorkie/blob/main/docs/design/mongodb-sharding.md
- [statement] Router targeting and local index selection are separate: mongos identifies candidate shards from shard-key metadata, while each contacted shard can use the most efficient eligible local index, including an index other than the shard-key index. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md
- [statement] Yorkie documents a concrete prefix-omission case: its Clients housekeeping query filters on _id and status but omits project_id, and the design explicitly labels it a scatter-gather query accepted for infrequent maintenance. The documented Clients key begins with project_id. (low confidence) — https://github.com/yorkie-team/yorkie/blob/main/docs/design/mongodb-sharding.md
- [statement] Percona demonstrates compound-key zone placement using a leading location field. This illustrates that constraining eligible placement requires configured zone ranges and assigned shards, beyond simply choosing a prefix that queries can target. (medium confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/sharding-with-zones-based-on-compound-shard-keys-on-mongodb-4-4/ · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md
- [statement] For {customerId:1,createdAt:1}, a customerId equality filter supports prefix targeting; a createdAt-only filter omits the prefix and generally requires scatter-gather. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-compound-shard-keys/view
- [statement] Design implication: leading tenant equality can preserve routing locality while suffix fields permit one tenant to span multiple chunks and shards. Yorkie explicitly describes splitting within a project using a compound key; prefix targeting therefore must not be treated as guaranteed tenant co-location. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://github.com/yorkie-team/yorkie/blob/main/docs/design/mongodb-sharding.md
- [statement] Choose fields around real query filters and aim to minimize shards contacted. Percona describes each shard as a coarse index and warns that an apparently transparent mongos query can hide expensive cross-shard execution. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md · keywords: Compound shard-key prefix targeting · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/choosing-a-good-sharding-key-in-mongodb-and-mysql/
